title: What the Sequence Cannot Say Alone — Germline Exomes & Genomes (H026), Karyotypes vs. Microarrays & Mosaicism (H027) & Veterinary Bone Marrow Architecture (V020)

teenKit.tldr: DNA sequencing isn't a magic truth machine that always gives clear answers; without the right tissue context, structural chromosome views, and species baseline, genetic tests can lead doctors wildly astray.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding the limits of medical testing helps us realize that science is an evolving detective story rather than a collection of absolute, error-free answers.
keyTakeaways: A genetic test result is only a single data point and means nothing without proper tissue and structural context.
Different tissues in the same body—like blood versus skin fibroblasts—can tell entirely different genetic stories due to mosaicism.
Applying medical baselines from one species, like dogs, directly to another species, like cats, can result in catastrophic diagnostic errors.

vocab.meaning: The complete set of protein-coding regions in an organism's DNA inherited from its parents.
An organized snapshot of a person's complete set of chromosomes, used to spot structural abnormalities.
A condition where a single individual has two or more genetically distinct cell populations derived from a single zygote.
A dangerous medical condition featuring a severe shortage of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets.

quiz.question: Why can testing only blood cells sometimes give a misleading genetic picture of a person's body?
options: Blood cells mutate every single hour.
Different tissues can have distinct genetic variations due to mosaicism that blood tests miss.
Blood cells do not contain any DNA.
Sequencers cannot read letters found in liquid tissue.
quiz.explanation: Mosaicism means different parts of the body can carry different genetic profiles, so looking at just one tissue type can hide crucial mutations.

quiz.question: What major lesson does the episode highlight about modern DNA sequencing?
options: It is completely infallible and replaces the need for doctors.
It works identically across every animal species on Earth.
It is a powerful tool, but a sequence alone is meaningless without proper biological context.
It can instantly diagnose broken bones just like an x-ray.
quiz.explanation: The episode emphasizes that DNA sequences are just data points that require structural, tissue, and species context to be interpreted correctly.

quiz.question: Why is 'One Medicine' thinking—comparing human and veterinary pathology—so critical?
options: Animals never get the same diseases as humans.
Mistaking a cat's normal biological baseline for a dog's can cause massive diagnostic mistakes.
Veterinary medicine never uses genetic testing.
Human genetic tests always work on cats and dogs.
quiz.explanation: Assuming different species share identical cellular architectures and baselines leads to dangerous medical errors.
